name: Highlands 3

nadir.desc: The nadir view shows a rural residential compound set on high desert terrain with sparse shrub and juniper vegetation across the surrounding parcel|The compound consists of multiple structures including a primary residence, at least one detached structure to the northwest, and a smaller outbuilding to the south, all connected by paved or hard-surface internal driveways|A blue sport court is visible on the west side of the compound, and a small turf or lawn area is present adjacent to the main structure|A single paved access road curves from the public road at the south, looping up and into the compound, with the main public road (Macalpine Loop) visible along the eastern and southern edges of the imagery.

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front of the property from the street side, revealing the primary residence and at least one secondary structure positioned centrally on the parcel with open desert terrain extending in front|A curved driveway is visible approaching the structures from the front, surfaced with a light-colored compacted material|Scattered juniper trees and rock outcroppings are present throughout the approach area but do not block the driveway path|The structures have low-pitch dark rooflines and light-colored exterior walls.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the property from the right side, with the curved access road clearly visible on the right edge of the frame connecting the compound to the public road below|The terrain on the right side of the property is open and relatively flat desert, providing unobstructed sightlines from the access road to the structures|Multiple structures are visible in the upper-left portion of this view, with juniper trees interspersed around the compound perimeter|No fencing or gates are observed along the right side approach.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, where dense juniper and scrub vegetation is concentrated along the back and left rear edges of the compound|The rear of the primary structures is visible with a light-colored outbuilding or wing extending to the south-southwest|The terrain to the rear rises slightly and is heavily vegetated with junipers, which would limit vehicle access and visibility from the rear|No rear access road or gate is visible from this perspective.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property, where the main structure with its dark roof is prominent in the foreground and a secondary structure with a lighter roof is visible to the right|The curved driveway is visible in the upper portion of the frame connecting to the compound from the north|Dense juniper vegetation borders the left side of the compound, with scrub desert extending further to the left and south|No fence line or secondary access point is visible on the left side.

considerations: The property is accessed by a single curved paved road off Macalpine Loop, which represents the only confirmed vehicular approach route; there is no visible secondary access from the rear or sides. Dense juniper and scrub vegetation along the rear and left sides of the compound limits responder movement, visibility, and staging in those areas. The open terrain on the right side and the front approach provide the best areas for apparatus staging and access. The sport court surface on the west side of the compound may offer an additional flat hard surface for staging if the driveway becomes congested.
clarifications: Is the driveway surface rated to support the weight of heavy emergency apparatus such as fire engines or ladder trucks? Are there any gates or access control devices at the road entrance to the driveway off Macalpine Loop? Are any of the detached structures locked, and do they contain hazardous materials such as fuel, propane, or chemicals? Is there a designated address marker or reflective signage visible from the public road at the driveway entrance? Are there any buried utilities, septic systems, or well infrastructure in the open areas around the structures that would affect vehicle positioning?
